## The course purpose

Build a research practice in which you can explain the technology, inspect delegated work, and retain responsibility for consequential decisions.


## Understanding

Distinguish **architecture**, **training**, **inference**, and the **application** around a model.

Use that account to explain both broad capability and convincing mistakes.


## Application

Create an organized research workspace.

Choose a task you need, define its boundaries, and produce an output with evidence of verification.


## Human control

People own the question, method, interpretation, and claims.

Agents can implement approved procedures and contribute evidence or criticism.


## Course sequence

| Part | Focus |
|---|---|
| Introduction | Foundations and setup |
| 1 | Principles and human control |
| 2 | A useful research workflow |
| 3 | Control and upkeep |
| 4 | Data and societal governance |
| 5 | To be defined |


## Learning format

Each core section is planned around background materials, a **two-hour live call**, and a practice exercise.

The five core calls total **ten live hours**. Other work adds to that total.


## Final project

A reproducible pipeline covering data sourcing, question management, merging, analysis, visualization, and a website.

Its scope and acceptance criteria will be agreed with the instructor.


## Evidence and disagreement

Political inquiry belongs in the course.

Support a position with evidence, engage a serious counterargument, and explain uncertainty. Agreement with the instructor is not the learning objective.
